dedupe_keys.name: a b street traffic simulation and street planning software

description: A/B Street is open-source software to plan, simulate and communicate changes that make cities friendlier to walking, cycling and public transit. It simulates traffic, lets users edit streets and intersections, plan bike networks, design low-traffic neighbourhoods and explore 15-minute neighbourhoods through games. Maps are built from OpenStreetMap, so the tool works anywhere in the world. It was developed by the A/B Street project; the README's 2025 update says the work has since turned into several successor tools from A/B Street Ltd, among them the Network Planning Workspace for cycle networks, a low-traffic neighbourhood tool, Plan Your Active Travel Schemes for Active Travel England, a 15-minute neighbourhood tool, Severance Snape and od2net. Access: the code is free on GitHub under the Apache License 2.0, written as a Rust workspace, with builds for the web browser, Windows, Mac, Linux and FreeBSD (release 0.3.49 linked from the README). Caveats: the original simulator is no longer the focus of development, and results depend on the completeness of OpenStreetMap lane and signal tags in the chosen area. It supports agent-based traffic simulation of street changes, active mobility network planning and communication of scenarios. It complements OSMnx, the Propensity to Cycle Tool and BikeDNA catalogued here.
